Document: Hospital Saint Joseph Hospital of Valmontone Doctor Carlo Rinaldi Rheumatology Specialist Patient Paola Marchetti  The patient, aged 45, comes to the consultation due to deformities in the phalanges of the toes and fingers, as well as the presence of a tumor in the facial region.   The patient has a history of cleft lip and palate in childhood, which was surgically corrected. She does not report any other relevant medical history.   The physical examination shows that the patient has a triangular epiphysis in the proximal phalanx of the fifth toe, focal sclerosis in several phalanges, dysplasia of the distal phalanges of the thumb with a hole in the center, and the presence of an extramedullary plasma cell tumor in the facial region. In addition, the presence of twisted conjunctival vessels in both eyes is noted.   Following the clinical evaluation and the findings, the diagnosis of Paget's disease of bone is established, a chronic metabolic bone disease that affects bone formation and can cause bone deformities, bone tumors and complications in other organs.   Pharmacological treatment will be started to control the activity of the disease and periodic controls will be scheduled to monitor the patient's progress.  This report is issued at the request of the patient for follow-up with a rheumatology specialist.

Hospital Saint Felix Hospital Doctor Carla Fontana Specialist in Internal Medicine Patient Miriam Bianchi  The patient, a 35-year-old woman, comes to the consultation due to various symptoms that require medical evaluation.   The patient reports a family history of genetic diseases, including cardiac and neurological disorders. She has experienced cranial neuralgia on a recurring basis in recent months, as well as the presence of abundant nevi on her skin.   On physical examination, an atrial septal defect, café-au-lait spots on the iris, and pale skin coloration are observed. In addition, the presence of a dissecting aortic aneurysm is evident, which requires a detailed evaluation of her cardiovascular status.  Complementary studies Laboratory tests were performed that revealed elevated levels of alpha-fetoprotein in the amniotic fluid, suggesting the presence of an alteration in the mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation chain.   Based on the clinical findings and complementary studies, a genetic syndrome affecting multiple systems of the body, including the nervous, cardiovascular and cutaneous systems, is suspected.  Treatment plan A multidisciplinary evaluation will be coordinated with specialists in genetics, neurology, cardiology and dermatology to establish a comprehensive management plan and provide the necessary support to the patient.

Hospital Saint Joseph Hospital of Valmontone Doctor Carlo Rinaldi Patient Carlo Ferrari The patient presents with persistent cough, difficulty breathing, fever, fatigue, loss of taste and smell, and body aches. Upon examination, the patient displays signs of respiratory distress, with increased respiratory rate and decreased oxygen saturation levels. Laboratory tests reveal elevated white blood cell count and inflammatory markers. Chest X-ray reveals bilateral infiltrates consistent with pneumonia. Given the clinical presentation and radiographic findings, it is likely that the patient has contracted a respiratory viral infection, possibly COVID-19, necessitating further evaluation and management.

Hospital Saint Lucy Hospital Doctor Maria Rizzo Specialist in Medical Genetics Patient Beatrice Guerra  A 25-year-old female patient comes to the clinic for multiple congenital abnormalities. The main abnormalities found include missing teeth, complete dermal syndactyly on fingers 3-4 of the hand, presence of facial hair on the cheeks, underdevelopment of the clitoris, hammer on the third toe, and central scotoma. These abnormalities have been present since birth and have caused concern in the patient.   The absence of several teeth in the oral cavity, complete dermal syndactyly on the left hand, presence of facial hair on the cheeks, underdeveloped clitoris, deformity in the third toe, and central scotoma are observed in the ophthalmological examination.   The possibility of a rare genetic syndrome that encompasses all the clinical manifestations present in the patient is raised. A genetic study is required to confirm the diagnosis.   The patient will be referred to the genetics service for specific tests to identify the etiology of the congenital anomalies present.  A check-up appointment is scheduled in one month to assess the results of genetic studies and establish a therapeutic plan.

Hospital Saint Peter Hospital of Rimini Doctor Alessandra Ferri Specialist in Medical Genetics Patient Caterina Bruno  The patient, 35 years old, comes to the consultation due to color blindness in cones, renal duplication, hook-shaped epiphysis of the middle phalanx of the second toe, progressive flexion deformity of the forearm and Potter's facial appearance. Hospital Saint Felix Hospital Doctor Enrico Santoro Internal Medicine Specialist Patient Francesco Parisi  The patient, 45 years old, comes to the consultation due to a series of symptoms that require detailed medical evaluation.   The patient reports a history of incipient cirrhosis and polycythemia vera previously diagnosed. In addition, a malformation of the striatum nucleus, alteration of emotional behavior, underdevelopment of the fovea, malformation of the malar bones and absence of the helix cross have been observed in the physical examination.   The patient is observed to have mild jaundice, cutaneous-mucosal pallor, gait disturbances and abnormal eye movements.  Complementary studies Blood tests were performed showing elevated liver enzyme and hematocrit values, as well as imaging studies confirming the aforementioned brain and bone malformations.   The patient's clinical picture is consistent with a rare disease of genetic origin that affects multiple body systems, including the liver, bone marrow, central nervous system, and vision.   A multidisciplinary treatment will be initiated that will include management of liver complications, control of polycythemia, neurological and ophthalmological follow-up, as well as psychological support for the patient and his family.  Periodic check-ups are scheduled to evaluate the evolution of the disease and adjust treatment as necessary.

Hospital Saint Joseph Hospital of Valmontone Doctor Silvia Bianchi Specialist in Internal Medicine Patient Chiara Bruno Barcelona Central Hospital  Clinical Report  Patient Ana  Medical Record Number 123456789 Date May 15, 2023   The patient, a 35-year-old woman, comes to the consultation due to a series of symptoms that require medical evaluation.   The patient has no relevant medical history. She has no history of kidney disease or known congenital malformations.   On physical examination, hydronephrosis is observed in the right kidney, suggesting a possible obstruction in the urinary tract. In addition, a decrease in the number of granulocytes is evident in the blood count. At the musculoskeletal level, grade I microtia is observed in the left ear, as well as an equinovarus deformity in the right foot and absence of distal phalanges in the toes of said foot.   1. Right hydronephrosis secondary to possible urinary tract obstruction. 2. Decreased granulocytes, suggestive of neutropenia. 3. Grade I microtia in the left ear. 4. Equinovarus deformity in the right foot. 5. Absence of distal phalanges in the toes of the right foot.  Treatment Plan Additional studies will be performed to determine the cause of the hydronephrosis and neutropenia. The patient will be referred to the corresponding specialists for the management of the identified congenital malformations.  A check-up appointment is scheduled in two weeks for follow-up and evaluation of results.

Hospital Saint Bartholomew Hospital Doctor Chiara Romano Specialist in Internal Medicine Patient Nicola Serra  The patient, 45 years old, comes to the consultation due to various symptoms that have been appearing progressively in recent weeks.   The patient reports pain in the left elbow when making movements, tachycardia of unknown origin, muscle weakness and alterations in the nails of the hands. In addition, a malignant tumor has been observed in the endometrium, changes in the fundus and hypertrophy in the proximal phalanx of the feet. Hospital Saint Lucy Hospital Doctor Maria Rizzo Neurology Specialist Patient Paolo Lombardi  The patient, 35 years old, comes to the consultation due to neurological and endocrine symptoms. He reports total loss of vibratory sensitivity in the lower limbs, permanent flexion of the fingers and difficulty with mobility. In addition, oligoasthenoteratozoospermia has been observed in the fertility study.   The patient has no relevant medical history. He does not report alcohol, tobacco or drug use.   The examination shows decreased vibratory sensitivity in the lower limbs, permanent flexion of the fingers, as well as signs of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.  Complementary studies Hormonal tests were performed that confirm the presence of hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction. In addition, retinoschisis was diagnosed in the ophthalmological evaluation.   The patient presents a clinical picture compatible with a neurological and endocrine pathology, suggestive of a possible genetic disease.   Symptomatic treatment will be started and the patient will be referred to a genetics consultation for molecular study.  A report will be issued for follow-up by the primary care physician.

Hospital Saint Michael Clinic Doctor Laura Ferri Internal Medicine Specialist Patient Dario Rizzo  The patient, aged 45, comes to the consultation presenting bone deformities in different parts of his body, as well as visual problems and a medical condition that has led to a recent sex change. In addition, punctate sclerosis is observed on the skin and a chest disease that affects his respiratory capacity.   During the physical examination, a fragmented and uneven-looking epiphysis is evident in several joints, including the absence of the epiphysis on the big toe. Likewise, degeneration of retinal cones is detected that affects the patient's vision. The distal humerus is hypotrophic, which could be related to the observed bone deformities.   A rare genetic disease is suspected that affects multiple body systems, including the skeleton, vision, and skin. Additional genetic studies are required to confirm the diagnosis.   Multidisciplinary follow-up will be initiated with specialists in genetics, ophthalmology, endocrinology and orthopedic surgery to comprehensively address the different manifestations of this disease.

Hospital Saint Felix Hospital Doctor Andrea De Rosa Neurology Specialist Patient Carlo Marchetti  The patient, 65 years old, comes to the consultation due to progressive weakness in the upper and lower limbs, as well as difficulty walking. In addition, he reports pain in the left hip and problems controlling urination.   After physical examination, evident muscle atrophy is observed in both upper and lower limbs. A disproportionate displacement of the medial femoral condyle in the left hip is noted. Likewise, sclerosis of the external urethral sphincter is detected.   Given the symptoms and clinical findings described, a possible degenerative neuromuscular disease is suspected. Complementary studies are required to confirm the diagnosis.   Symptomatic treatment is started to improve the patient's quality of life, including physical therapy and pain management. Periodic follow-up is scheduled to evaluate the evolution of the disease.

Hospital Saint Lucy Hospital Doctor Francesca Puglisi Specialist in Internal Medicine Patient Armando Rizzo  The patient, 45 years old, comes to the consultation due to a prominent frontal protuberance, an abnormality in the heart with a split atrial septum, dacryocystopathy, and duplication of the pelvis of the kidney. The frontal protuberance has become evident in recent months and has caused concern in the patient. Likewise, alterations in the structure of the heart and abnormalities in the urinary system have been observed.   Upon inspection, the presence of a frontal protuberance of firm consistency is evident, the patient reports pain on palpation in the area. Upon auscultation of the heart, heart murmurs are appreciated and the presence of a split atrial septum is confirmed. In the ocular region, epiphora and redness are observed, suggestive of dacryocystopathy. In addition, a mass is palpated in the lumbar region, compatible with duplication of the pelvis of the kidney.   The possibility of a rare genetic disease affecting multiple systems, such as Pallister-Hall Syndrome, is raised. Genetic studies and complementary tests are required to confirm the diagnosis.   A multidisciplinary follow-up will be initiated with specialists in genetics, cardiology, ophthalmology and urology to comprehensively address the manifestations of this pathology.

Hospital Saint Francis Hospital Doctor Stefano Marino Specialist in Clinical Genetics Patient Cristian Mariani  The patient, aged 45, comes to the consultation due to a series of symptoms that have been progressing in recent weeks. The main symptoms include the presence of two phalanges in the third toe, generalized hair loss, fragmented epiphyses of the proximal phalanges of the hand, malformation of the third ventricle, downward eye movements, acute gastroenteritis and dysplasia of the dermal melanosomes.   On physical examination, the presence of additional phalanges in the third toe, generalized alopecia, deformities in the proximal phalanges of the hand, alterations in the morphology of the third ventricle, abnormal eye movements, signs of acute gastrointestinal irritation and alterations in dermal pigmentation are observed.   After evaluating the symptoms and performing a physical examination, a rare genetic syndrome is suspected that affects multiple body systems, including the skeletal, central nervous, ocular, gastrointestinal and dermal systems.   Genetic studies will be performed to confirm the diagnosis and a multidisciplinary treatment will be prescribed to address the different clinical manifestations present in the patient.  Follow-up The patient will be scheduled for follow-up in the next few weeks to assess the evolution of his/her clinical condition and adjust the treatment as necessary.

Hospital Saint Benedict Polyclinic Doctor Sofia Ricci Specialist in Pediatrics Patient Paola Monti  2-year-old patient with a history of delayed eruption of baby teeth and an undeveloped nose. She has immobility of the small joints of the foot, abnormal epiphyses of the second toe, ventricular dysrhythmias, atonic epilepsy, and polymorphic focal epileptiform discharges. Radiological and electroencephalographic studies are performed to evaluate the patient's current condition. Episodes of disorientation and loss of consciousness are evident.   A rare genetic disorder affecting bone, dental, and neurological development is suspected. Hospital Saint Benedict Polyclinic Doctor Marco Galli Specialist in Internal Medicine Patient Beatrice Rinaldi  The patient, 35 years old, comes to the consultation due to difficulty understanding spoken language, as well as vision abnormalities such as tortuous retinal vessels.   Mrs. García has had a previous premature birth due to early rupture of fetal membranes.   During the physical examination, fragmented subungual hyperkeratosis is observed in several nails, enlarged phalanges on the ring finger, aplasia/hypoplasia of the bones of the big toe, irregularity in the metaphysis of the proximal humerus and signs of possible arterial embolism. Hospital Saint Martin Hospital of Rivabella Doctor Luigi Esposito Specialist in Medical Genetics Patient Tommaso Messina Number 123456789 Date September 15, 2023   The patient comes to the outpatient clinic due to abnormalities in the glabella, anterior protrusions in the tongue of the lumbar vertebrae, benign fat masses in different areas of the body, increased fluid throughout the body, metaphysis with irregular contours, bone sclerosis in the phalanx of the fifth finger and pseudoepiphyseal epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the fourth finger of the hand.   The patient is observed to have the aforementioned abnormalities, as well as limitation in the mobility of the lumbar spine and deformity in the affected fingers.   A possible genetic condition is suspected that affects bone development and the distribution of adipose tissue in the body. Additional studies are required to confirm the diagnosis.  Treatment Plan X-rays, MRIs, and genetic analysis will be requested to determine the underlying cause of the observed abnormalities. The patient will be referred to the Medical Genetics service for comprehensive management of his or her condition.  A follow-up appointment is scheduled in one month to review the results and follow up on the case.

Hospital Saint Charles Hospital of Alba Doctor Daniele Costa Specialist in Medical Genetics Patient Giovanni Giordano  The patient, 30 years old, comes to the consultation due to deformities in the phalanges of the hands, hearing disorders and other physical alterations.   The patient has a history of Klinefelter Syndrome, which is characterized by the presence of an additional X chromosome in males, which can cause various alterations in physical and reproductive development.   On physical examination, an abnormality is observed in the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the fourth finger of the hand, as well as digital synostosis and ivory epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the third finger of the hand. In addition, a mild to moderate hearing disorder and features of acromegaloidism, such as enlarged hands and feet, are evident.   After the clinical evaluation and the findings found, the diagnosis of Klinefelter Syndrome with manifestations of acromegaloidism is established.   Follow-up with the genetics and endocrinology team is recommended for comprehensive management of the condition, as well as an evaluation by otorhinolaryngology to address the hearing disorder.

Hospital Saint Teresa Polyclinic Doctor Giulia Galli Specialist in Internal Medicine Patient Giuseppe Rossi  The patient, aged 45, comes to the consultation due to a complex clinical picture. He reports difficulty in flexing the elbow, distal peripheral sensory neuropathy and alterations in the humerus. In addition, semilobar brain malformations have been observed in previous imaging tests. Likewise, the patient has suffered repeated infections by Streptococcus pneumoniae, testicular hypoplasia, spongiform encephalopathy and lactic acidosis.   On examination, signs of testicular hypoplasia and difficulty in flexing the elbow are evident. Alterations in the humerus and distal peripheral sensory neuropathy are also observed.   In light of this clinical picture, the possibility of a rare genetic syndrome affecting multiple systems of the body, including the central nervous system, the musculoskeletal system and the immune system, is raised.   Genetic studies will be carried out to confirm the diagnosis and a multidisciplinary treatment will be prescribed that will include neurological, endocrinological and genetic monitoring.  A check-up appointment is made in one month for control and follow-up of the patient.

Hospital Sun Queen Hospital Doctor Marco Vitale Internal Medicine Specialist Patient Giuliano Fabbri  The patient, 10 years old, comes to the consultation due to a series of congenital anomalies and findings in complementary studies.   The patient has previously been diagnosed with epiphysis sclerosis and proximal radial epiphysis agenesis.   The MRI shows an enlargement of the two cerebral ventricles. In addition, stenosis of the ureterovesical junction is evident in the renal ultrasound.  Results of complementary studies The EEG shows the presence of temporal spike-wave discharges. Likewise, an anterior anus is identified in the physical examination and a narrow palpebral fissure in adduction in the ophthalmological examination. Finally, the presence of abnormal insertion tendons in the mitral valve is confirmed in the echocardiogram.   1. Sclerosis of the epiphysis 2. Agenesis of the proximal radial epiphysis 3. Abnormal insertion of tendons in the mitral valve  Treatment plan A multidisciplinary follow-up will be carried out with specialists in neurology, urology, plastic surgery, ophthalmology and cardiology to comprehensively address the various alterations present in the patient.
